papers.title: FutureWorld: A Plug-and-Play Causal Next-State Predictor for Interactive Video World Exploration
papers.abstract: Interactive video world models aim to follow user actions while maintaining scene consistency over extended interactions. History-based methods reuse generated latents to preserve scene content, but three limitations of this reuse contribute to error recirculation. 1) The latent generated at each interaction is retained as history, potentially containing blurred details, geometric distortions, or semantic drift. 2) Although retrieved historical content matches the current scene, it can still contain errors that are carried into the next chunk. 3) New outputs then become history for later interactions, potentially reinforcing the same errors through repeated reuse. To limit this cycle, we aim to predict the future scene state from the current generated latent and the next action before generating the next interaction's video chunk. This future-state prior provides guidance for the next chunk, with the aim of reducing the errors carried forward from history. To this end, we propose a plug-and-play Causal Next-Chunk Predictor (C-NCP) with cross-model adaptability and prediction-guided modulation. We integrate C-NCP into four base generators and evaluate the augmented models across three benchmarks for interactive long-video generation and action-conditioned world modeling. Extensive experiments demonstrate reduced error accumulation and improved long-horizon consistency across diverse generation settings. The project page is at https://GuangYuanKK.github.io/futureworld.
papers.summary_cn: 论文针对交互式视频世界模型中历史潜变量反复复用导致的错误循环传播问题，提出 FutureWorld。其核心是因果下一视频块预测器 C-NCP：根据当前生成潜变量和下一动作，预测完整的下一潜变量块，并通过通道级残差调制将这一未来状态先验注入冻结的自回归视频 DiT。C-NCP 使用 VAE 特定输入适配器和输出头适配不同生成器，采用因果时空注意力、动作条件以及包含时间差分监督的两阶段训练，以适应预测反馈。作者将其集成到 Matrix-Game 3.0、HY-World 1.5、LingBot-World-Fast 和 SANA-WM，在 Sekai、RealEstate10K 和 WBench 上进行评估。结果显示，增强模型在视觉质量、运动平滑度、主体与背景一致性等指标上普遍优于基础模型，并改善了 60 秒交互式 rollout 的场景保持能力；在 Matrix-Game 3.0 上，额外推理开销约为每次交互 0.617 秒，即 9.24%。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出面向交互式视频生成错误循环传播的未来状态引导校正范式，在下一视频块生成前根据当前状态和下一动作重新估计未来状态，而不是仅复用历史内容。2. 设计即插即用的因果下一视频块预测器 C-NCP，通过 VAE 特定适配器和共享时空预测主干支持跨模型潜变量表示，并通过因果时序预测符合自回归生成方向。3. 提出预测引导的通道级残差调制，将预测未来状态以保持张量形状的方式注入基础生成器，同时结合动作条件和时间差分损失。4. 采用先使用真实信息辅助、再使用预测反馈的两阶段训练策略，并将方法集成到四个基础世界模型，在三个基准上验证其对长时域一致性和错误累积的改善。
papers.relevance_cn: 该工作与研究重点高度相关：它面向动作条件视觉世界模型和闭环交互式模拟，在每次交互中根据下一动作预测未来场景状态，并将生成结果反馈为下一轮输入。方法采用自回归、因果的下一视频块预测，适用于长视频和流式分块生成；其因果时空注意力使未来切片只能依赖当前状态、动作和此前切片。它还直接研究历史复用造成的误差累积，并通过预测先验和调制机制进行纠正。论文涉及缓存或历史内容复用，但重点不是稀疏注意力、蒸馏或缓存压缩；其主要效率结果是预测器带来约 9.24% 的推理时间开销，而非实现实时生成加速。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确表明，理论分析基于平方误差，并不等同于所使用的归一化混合损失的精确最优性，也没有给出 rollout 误差收缩的保证。预测器在 Sekai 上训练，尽管在其他数据集上测试并取得提升，但跨数据分布的泛化范围仍有限。实验视频主要为 60 秒，论文未明确说明在更长时域上的性能上限。方法需要为不同 VAE 和生成器配置适配器，并额外进行预测，因此会增加推理时间；论文仅报告了 Matrix-Game 3.0、四个 720P 视频块和 A800 GPU 条件下的开销。实验只覆盖四个基础生成器和所列三个基准，尚不能说明对更广泛架构、动作空间或真实闭环环境的适用性。论文未明确说明预测未来状态的不确定性建模、失败检测机制，以及在动作分布显著偏离训练数据时的表现。
papers.abstract_cn: 交互式视频世界模型旨在遵循用户动作，同时在长时间交互中保持场景一致性。基于历史的方法会复用生成的潜变量以保留场景内容，但这种复用存在三个会导致错误循环传播的局限。1）每次交互生成的潜变量都会被保留为历史，其中可能包含细节模糊、几何失真或语义漂移。2）即使检索到的历史内容与当前场景相匹配，其中仍可能包含会被带入下一个视频块的错误。3）新的输出随后又会成为后续交互的历史，从而可能通过反复复用强化相同的错误。为限制这一循环，我们希望在生成下一次交互的视频块之前，根据当前生成的潜变量和下一步动作预测未来场景状态。该未来状态先验为下一视频块提供引导，旨在减少从历史中延续的错误。为此，我们提出了即插即用的因果下一视频块预测器（C-NCP），具备跨模型适应性和预测引导调制能力。我们将 C-NCP 集成到四个基础生成器中，并在三个交互式长视频生成和动作条件世界建模基准上评估增强后的模型。大量实验表明，该方法减少了错误累积，并在多种生成设置下提升了长时域一致性。项目主页：https://GuangYuanKK.github.io/futureworld。

papers.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
papers.abstract: Interactive world models generate visual content conditioned on user actions, yet maintaining spatial consistency over long-horizon exploration in real time remains challenging. Existing approaches rely on either temporal context or explicit 3D memory, both of which scale poorly because memory grows with the length of the generated stream. Moreover, explicit 3D memories condition latent video generators by re-encoding RGB renderings, which precludes real-time generation. In this paper, we introduce a Latent 3D Gaussian Memory (L3G) that combines the efficiency of feed-forward reconstruction with a compact, rapidly renderable scene representation. Building on this memory, we propose L3G-World, in which a memory updater and a video diffusion transformer (DiT) alternate autoregressively to generate spatially consistent worlds. The memory updater spawns Gaussians in newly observed regions and refines existing ones, so that the memory grows with scene extent rather than stream length. Each Gaussian further stores a VAE latent feature, allowing the memory to be rendered directly into the DiT's latent space without VAE re-encoding. Experiments show that L3G-World achieves state-of-the-art generation quality and long-horizon spatial consistency, with up to $38.6\times$ fewer 3D primitives, $3.2\times$ faster memory updates, and $359\times$ faster memory rendering relative to the most efficient prior 3D-memory baseline for each metric, enabling real-time world generation at 9 FPS.
papers.summary_cn: L3G-World 面向从单张图像和相机轨迹实时生成可探索、空间一致的长时域世界。系统由 L3G-Mem 和 L3G-Gen 组成：前者使用可持续更新的潜在三维高斯记忆，仅在未覆盖区域生成高斯并对已有高斯进行残差细化；后者将记忆中的 VAE 特征直接渲染到潜空间，作为视频扩散 Transformer 生成下一视频块的条件。二者交替构成自回归闭环，并通过少步蒸馏实现实时推理。在 DL3DV 和 RealEstate10K 上，方法在长时域一致性、生成质量和记忆效率方面总体优于多种时间上下文及显式三维记忆基线，完整模型可达到约 9 FPS。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出潜在三维高斯记忆，将紧凑的三维场景表示与可直接渲染的 VAE 潜特征结合，避免 RGB 渲染后的 VAE 重编码。 2. 提出 L3G-Mem，通过自适应生成新高斯和细化已有高斯，使记忆规模主要随场景空间范围增长，而不是随生成流长度累积。 3. 提出由 L3G-Mem 与记忆条件视频 DiT 交替组成的 L3G-World 自回归生成框架，以持久三维记忆支持长时域空间一致性和回环闭合。 4. 使用少步、在策略蒸馏降低视频生成采样成本，实现单张图像条件下约 9 FPS 的实时世界生成。 5. 在两个数据集上进行了生成质量、自一致性、三维一致性、相机控制和记忆效率评估，并通过消融验证自适应生成、记忆细化、全局自注意力和 VAE 潜特征提升的作用。
papers.relevance_cn: 本文与研究重点高度相关。它属于动作或相机轨迹条件的交互式视觉世界模型，通过自回归视频扩散生成器根据目标相机运动持续生成环境，可用于闭环世界模拟。其核心贡献直接涉及长视频和流式生成：以视频块为单位交替更新记忆与生成内容，并通过持久三维记忆避免时间上下文随序列长度线性增长。它还针对实时生成，采用少步扩散蒸馏，并通过潜空间直接渲染、稀疏且紧凑的高斯记忆和自适应更新降低推理、存储及渲染开销。论文报告完整系统约 9.02 FPS，表明其对实时交互和可扩展长时域生成具有直接价值。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文未设置单独的局限性讨论，但实验和方法描述表明存在以下限制：1. 评估主要基于 DL3DV 和 RealEstate10K，以及从单张输入图像出发的预设相机轨迹，尚未充分证明在更广泛真实环境、复杂用户动作或真正无限时长下的表现。2. 系统仍依赖几何基础模型、VAE 和视频 DiT，训练和部署成本较高；论文的实时性能是在单张 NVIDIA H100 上报告的，硬件可迁移性未明确说明。3. 少步蒸馏版本相较完整模型在部分生成质量、自一致性和三维指标上有所下降。4. 尽管记忆主要随场景范围增长，持续探索更大或更复杂场景时，三维记忆仍会增长，且论文未明确给出其长期增长上限。5. L3G-World 在 RealEstate10K 的部分相机姿态和 MEt3R 几何指标并非最佳，说明实时性、生成质量、相机控制和几何一致性之间仍存在权衡。
papers.abstract_cn: 交互式世界模型根据用户动作生成视觉内容，但在实时条件下维持长时域探索中的空间一致性仍然具有挑战性。现有方法依赖时间上下文或显式三维记忆，而这两类方法都会因为记忆随生成流长度增长而难以扩展。此外，显式三维记忆通过重新编码 RGB 渲染结果来为潜空间视频生成器提供条件，这阻碍了实时生成。本文提出潜在三维高斯记忆（Latent 3D Gaussian Memory，L3G），将前馈重建的高效率与紧凑且可快速渲染的场景表示相结合。在此记忆的基础上，我们提出 L3G-World，其中记忆更新器与视频扩散 Transformer（DiT）以自回归方式交替运行，从而生成具有空间一致性的世界。记忆更新器在新观测区域生成高斯，并细化已有高斯，使记忆规模随场景范围而非生成流长度增长。每个高斯还存储一个 VAE 潜特征，使记忆能够直接渲染到 DiT 的潜空间中，无需通过 VAE 重新编码。实验表明，L3G-World 在生成质量和长时域自一致性方面达到了最先进水平；相较于每项指标中最高效的已有三维记忆基线，它最多可减少 38.6 倍三维基元，将记忆重建速度提高 3.2 倍，并将记忆渲染速度提高 359 倍，从而实现 9 FPS 的实时世界生成。

papers.title: Wizard: Manipulate Any World in Real Time via Agentic Control
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video world models have enabled the generation of increasingly realistic and interactive virtual environments, opening new possibilities for player-customizable gameplay. Agentic frameworks further advance this direction by decoupling explicit game logic and controllable world representations from visual generation. However, existing approaches support only simple game settings and predefined motion patterns, generalize poorly to unseen environments and characters, and offer limited real-time interactivity. In this paper, we introduce Wizard, an agentic game world model that enables real-time, precise control over character motions while generalizing zero-shot across novel scenes, characters, and actions. To achieve this, we construct a diverse dataset spanning 750 scenes and 178 characters, incorporating skeleton and geometry information as structured representations. We leverage these representations as intermediate proxies to condition a video generation model, together with an adaptive masking mechanism that improves alignment between the conditioning signals and generated video rollouts. Furthermore, we introduce an agentic framework that explicitly maintains and updates game states, allowing players to freely configure their virtual worlds and exercise fine-grained control over character motions while preserving visual quality and gameplay consistency. By combining agentic control with structured proxy-based generation, our framework unlocks new possibilities for player-driven game creation with real-time, generalizable, and mechanically consistent world simulation.
papers.summary_cn: Wizard是一个面向可定制游戏世界的智能体视频世界模型。系统从用户提供的场景图像和角色图像重建近似3D场景几何与可控角色骨骼，并通过动作检索和重定向生成目标角色的动作库。智能体显式维护角色位置、姿态、生命值、攻击阶段和冷却等世界状态，依据玩家输入和规则控制场景、角色及战斗逻辑，再将这些状态编码为几何与骨骼视觉代理，驱动基于Wan2.2-TI2V-5B的视频生成器。模型使用50.3小时、覆盖750个场景和178个角色的数据训练，并采用角色感知自适应注意力掩码、因果适配和少步蒸馏，在2步去噪、KV缓存条件下实现24 FPS的实时自回归生成。实验展示了对未见场景、角色和动作的零样本泛化，以及角色变换、场景操纵和符合机制的战斗交互。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出Wizard智能体游戏世界模型，通过结构化场景几何和关节骨骼实现角色与场景的细粒度控制、零样本泛化及符合游戏机制的实时交互。2. 构建覆盖750个场景、178个角色的50.3小时多源数据集，将视频与场景几何、角色骨骼进行对齐。3. 提出基于智能体的视频到视频框架，显式维护世界状态、规划行为并执行战斗规则。4. 提出基于骨骼位置的角色感知自适应注意力掩码，将角色参考图像绑定到对应空间区域，改善角色身份保持和参考图像与生成视频的对齐。5. 通过因果适配、少步蒸馏和有限窗口KV缓存，使视频生成器能够以2步去噪实现24 FPS的实时流式生成。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它直接研究视频生成驱动的交互式世界模型，并将玩家动作、自然语言场景编辑和角色动作转换为结构化几何与骨骼条件。其智能体显式跟踪世界状态、执行规则并将更新后的状态反馈给视频生成器，形成面向游戏的闭环模拟。方法采用因果适配、自回归生成、20个潜在帧的滑动上下文、持久注意力汇聚帧和KV缓存，针对长序列实时生成、有限内存流式推理和缓存复用进行了设计；少步蒸馏进一步支持24 FPS实时生成。论文还涉及动作条件控制、角色与场景的零样本泛化，以及通过稀疏的角色区域注意力掩码改善条件对齐。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出两项局限：第一，系统依赖动作库，对于具有罕见身体结构的角色，可能难以找到兼容动作；第二，在更长的视频推演中，场景代理与生成视频之间的一致性可能下降。论文还指出初始化阶段需要少于五分钟来重建场景、绑定角色骨骼并构建目标动作集。对于更长时间范围内的状态保持、与真实物理完全一致的模拟、以及全面定量的性能评估，论文未明确说明。
papers.abstract_cn: 近年来，视频世界模型的发展使虚拟环境的生成日益逼真且交互性更强，为玩家可定制的游戏玩法开辟了新的可能。智能体框架通过将显式游戏逻辑和可控的世界表示与视觉生成解耦，进一步推动了这一方向。然而，现有方法仅支持简单的游戏场景和预定义的运动模式，对未见过的环境和角色泛化能力较弱，实时交互能力也有限。本文提出Wizard，一种智能体游戏世界模型，能够实时、精确地控制角色运动，并以零样本方式泛化到新场景、新角色和新动作。为此，我们构建了一个涵盖750个场景和178个角色的多样化数据集，并将骨骼和几何信息纳入结构化表示。我们利用这些表示作为中间代理来条件化视频生成模型，同时引入自适应掩码机制，以改善条件信号与生成视频推演之间的对齐。此外，我们提出一种智能体框架，显式维护和更新游戏状态，使玩家能够自由配置虚拟世界，并对角色运动进行细粒度控制，同时保持视觉质量和游戏玩法一致性。通过结合智能体控制与基于结构化代理的生成，我们的框架为玩家驱动的游戏创作带来了新的可能，实现了实时、可泛化且符合游戏机制的世界模拟。

papers.title: UniWorld: A Unified World Model for Real-Time Visual World Simulation
papers.abstract: Continuous visual world simulation requires coupling evolving scene geometry with temporally persistent appearance. We present UniWorld, a unified framework that integrates depth trajectories and reference appearance within a shared video generation model. The central design maintains visual and geometric histories on a common timeline. Noise-aligned overlapping continuation places generated history at the prescribed sampling noise level and commits only newly generated latents. Rolling depth latent state preserves the corresponding geometric controls, incrementally reads newly available geometry, and keeps the conditioning fixed within each sampling window. Together, these mechanisms ensure exact preservation of latent history while bounding the active depth state by the window size. We evaluate continuous generation, paired history interventions, and long-horizon behavior across diverse scene categories. The same generator supports estimated, native, and on-demand simulator depth, while cached and incremental execution paths produce bitwise-identical outputs. Appearance changes and geometric control branches operate through the same interface without modifying committed history. The measured steady-state DiT execution path achieves real-time generation throughput, demonstrating the efficiency of UniWorld for continuous visual world simulation. Project page: https://zephipage.github.io/UniWorld.
papers.summary_cn: Continuous visual world simulation requires coupling evolving scene geometry with temporally persistent appearance.
papers.contribution_cn: We present UniWorld, a unified framework that integrates depth trajectories and reference appearance within a shared video generation model.
papers.relevance_cn: 匹配研究线：world model, efficient generation；关键词：world model, simulation, real-time, cache, video generation
papers.limitations_cn: 规则模式无法可靠判断实验质量与论文局限。

papers.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.
papers.summary_cn: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos.

papers.relevance_cn: 匹配研究线：world model, video generation；关键词：world model, video world model, action-conditioned, interactive, video generation

papers.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
papers.abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.

papers.contribution_cn: We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation.

papers.title: Hierarchical Diffusion for Camera-controlled Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: We address the task of long-video, camera-controlled generation from a single image. The dominant autoregressive paradigm suffers from two key limitations: (1) error accumulation over time, as distant frames are conditioned on previously generated outputs rather than ground truth, leading to drift; and (2) ambiguity in how to incorporate camera control. Standard solutions to both--such as self-forcing and conditioning on explicit 6-DOF poses--either incur significant computational overhead or produce drifting scene geometries over time. We propose a simple and lightweight framework that combines autoregressive generation (WanAR) with hierarchical long-context denoising (FixAR). To enforce scene geometry remains consistent with input cameras, we draw from feed-forward novel-view synthesis and reformulate video generation as a warping-and-inpainting problem. To mitigate drift, we introduce a hierarchical denoising strategy in which different stages condition on different temporal histories. Specifically, we first generate frames conditioned on the immediate past, and then refine them using a second denoiser conditioned on a temporally subsampled long-range history to enforce global consistency. This fine-to-coarse scheme enables each generated frame to effectively condition on the full temporal context without incurring a prohibitive cost. Experiments on RealEstate10k and DL3DV demonstrate that WanAR+FixAR outperforms prior methods for camera-controlled long-video generation, producing results that are both temporally stable and consistent with input camera trajectories.
papers.summary_cn: We address the task of long-video, camera-controlled generation from a single image.
papers.contribution_cn: We propose a simple and lightweight framework that combines autoregressive generation (WanAR) with hierarchical long-context denoising (FixAR).

papers.title: ReferStream: Interactive Subject Injection for Streaming Video Generation
papers.abstract: Injecting new subjects naturally during streaming video generation requires integrating newly supplied visual references into the existing video while preserving established subjects and the scene. Encoding references independently of the current scene provides little guidance for this integration, while keeping their features in persistent memory can interfere with established context. We propose ReferStream, a framework that requires no additional training and combines reference construction using the current scene with transient cache injection. Joint Latent places reference latents in target regions of the latest scene latent, allowing reference features to be extracted in context. Cache Restoration uses these features to condition the injection chunk, then restores the overwritten global cache entries while retaining the newly generated history. This procedure incorporates new visual conditions without retraining the generator or revising emitted frames. We further introduce ReferStream Bench, a new benchmark with scheduled reference arrivals, evolving instructions, and explicit annotations of subject presence for InShot and MultiShot generation. Evaluation follows the event schedule and measures both the fidelity of new subjects and the preservation of established subjects, alongside video quality, text adherence, and count accuracy. Experiments on ReferStream Bench show higher scores for text adherence, subject similarity, and count accuracy than the compared baselines, including offline methods given all references in advance. Project page: https://xushuolin.github.io/ReferStream/.

papers.title: Seeing and Imagining as One: Unified Video Generation and 4D Perception for Embodied World Modeling
papers.abstract: Embodied world models should not only imagine plausible futures, but also perceive the geometric, semantic, and motion structure of the evolving world. We present GenSight, a unified embodied world model that brings future video generation and dense perception into a single pretrained video diffusion transformer. GenSight uses a unified spatiotemporal representation for video, depth, embodiment segmentation, and first-frame-relative 2D flow. Built on a shared DiT backbone, GenSight uses lightweight task modulation to predict all modalities within the same architecture. All tasks are jointly optimized within a unified velocity prediction space. At inference, GenSight supports two complementary modes: multi-step future video generation with aligned dense predictions and single-step dense perception from an observed video. By unifying modality representation, model architecture, and prediction space, GenSight avoids separate modality-specific pipelines and couples appearance, geometry, semantics, and motion in a shared representation. It promotes cross-modal consistency and allows dense perception to benefit from the spatiotemporal priors learned through video generation. Trained on embodied manipulation data spanning multiple robot embodiments and human-hand interactions, GenSight demonstrates strong performance in both video generation and dense 4D perception, highlighting the effectiveness of unifying seeing and imagining for embodied world modeling.

papers.title: WorldFlow: Joint Video and 3D Motion Prediction via Large-Scale Pretraining
papers.abstract: Predicting future physical states stands as a central challenge in embodied intelligence. Existing video world models leave 3D dynamics implicit, action-based formulations remain tied to specific robot configurations, and 3D motion prediction models use flow-only supervision, providing a limited learning signal for physical dynamics. To circumvent these limitations, we introduce \method{}, a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and query-based 3D trajectories. By parameterizing 3D motion as continuous displacement tokens aligned with the video grid, a unified Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone jointly denoises both modalities under a rectified-flow objective. This formulation couples explicit geometric dynamics with visual evolution, effectively unlocking the physical commonsense embedded within pretrained video models. To empirically scale and validate this unified architecture, we train \method{} on a heterogeneous mixture of 1.44 million object-level samples spanning simulated and real-world domains. We further introduce WorldFlowBench, comprising 1,678 evaluation samples from 11 data sources across simulated and real-world interactions, including spatial reasoning tasks. Across all three evaluation sets, WorldFlow achieves the lowest average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) among the evaluated learning-based methods. Notably, on the challenging SpatialCog set, WorldFlow achieves an ADE of 0.060 m, a 54.2\% reduction compared with the strongest external baseline. It also reduces ADE and FDE by 55.9\% and 68.5\%, respectively, compared with its flow-only variant. Project page: https://worldflow-rbs.github.io/.
